title: Design network segmentation and trust zones: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: Where should this flow cross a trust boundary, what policy permits it, and how will a bypass or failure be detected?
focalInsight: A zone is a defined trust purpose plus enforced, observable crossings; VLANs and tunnels are mechanisms, not the purpose itself.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Trust Zone
nodes.definition: Grouping with a stated trust/business purpose, assets, identities, permitted flows, owners, and failure consequences.
nodes.detail: Grouping with a stated trust/business purpose, assets, identities, permitted flows, owners, and failure consequences.
nodes.decision: Create a zone when its trust requirement differs; document crossings and exceptions.
nodes.failureExample: An undefined “secure zone” cannot support consistent allow/deny decisions.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A zone needs purpose, assets, identities, crossings, and owner.

nodes.label: Network Segmentation
nodes.definition: Physical or logical restriction of communication between zones to reduce reachability and blast radius.
nodes.detail: Physical or logical restriction of communication between zones to reduce reachability and blast radius.
nodes.decision: Place enforcement on real crossings and test allowed, denied, and failure behavior.
nodes.failureExample: A segmented diagram with an unfiltered routing path leaves lateral movement intact.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Segmentation works only at enforced crossings.

nodes.label: Micro Segmentation
nodes.definition: Workload/identity-level policy that limits east-west communication beyond coarse network zones.
nodes.detail: Workload/identity-level policy that limits east-west communication beyond coarse network zones.
nodes.decision: Use for high-value or mixed-trust workloads; maintain service identity, policy lifecycle, and telemetry.
nodes.failureExample: One compromised pod reaches peer services because the whole subnet is allowed.

nodes.label: Traffic Flows
nodes.definition: Specified source, destination, service, direction, identity, and path relationships that a zone policy evaluates.
nodes.detail: Specified source, destination, service, direction, identity, and path relationships that a zone policy evaluates.
nodes.decision: Inventory before policy; remove stale flows and verify dependency changes.
nodes.failureExample: A forgotten backup path becomes an unmonitored bridge across zones.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A flow description states who talks to what, why, and through which enforcement.

nodes.label: Zero Trust
nodes.definition: Design approach that continuously evaluates identity, device/context, and policy rather than assuming network location grants trust.
nodes.detail: Design approach that continuously evaluates identity, device/context, and policy rather than assuming network location grants trust.
nodes.decision: Apply explicit verification and least privilege at each requested resource/action while planning availability and telemetry.
nodes.failureExample: A user on a corporate subnet receives broad access because location is treated as sufficient trust.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Zero trust verifies access per request/context, not merely network location.

nodes.label: Vlan
nodes.definition: Layer-2 logical LAN segmentation on switching infrastructure.
nodes.detail: Layer-2 logical LAN segmentation on switching infrastructure.
nodes.decision: Use with inter-VLAN routing/ACL policy, trunk controls, management protection, and monitoring.
nodes.failureExample: Putting systems in different VLANs without controlling the router between them does not block communication.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A VLAN separates Layer-2 broadcast domains; Layer-3 policy still matters.

nodes.label: VPN
nodes.definition: Protected logical tunnel connecting users/sites/networks through defined endpoints and traffic selectors.
nodes.detail: Protected logical tunnel connecting users/sites/networks through defined endpoints and traffic selectors.
nodes.decision: Verify authentication, endpoint trust, split/full routing, authorization, logs, and termination boundary.
nodes.failureExample: A VPN grants a remote device broad internal reachability despite lacking device posture.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: A VPN is a protected path, not blanket trust.

nodes.label: Vrf
nodes.definition: Virtual routing/forwarding instances that keep route tables and forwarding domains logically separate.
nodes.detail: Virtual routing/forwarding instances that keep route tables and forwarding domains logically separate.
nodes.decision: Use for tenant/site separation while controlling route leaking, management, and monitoring.
nodes.failureExample: An unintended route leak connects two customer/zone routing domains.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: VRF separates routing tables; review route-leak exceptions.

nodes.label: Air Gap
nodes.definition: Physical/logical separation intended to remove ordinary network paths between environments.
nodes.detail: Physical/logical separation intended to remove ordinary network paths between environments.
nodes.decision: Use only with controlled transfer, maintenance, media, and verification procedures; validate no hidden bridge exists.
nodes.failureExample: A dual-homed maintenance laptop silently bridges an “air-gapped” environment.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Air gap reduces paths; transfer/maintenance paths remain security decisions.
